Just pasting from Gemini, but makes perfect sense: 

Closed-mouth thumbnails increase watch time because they attract a more targeted, genuine audience rather than casual scrollers chasing a cheap clickbait shock.

The Behavioral and Psychological Factors

• Authenticity vs. Exaggeration: Open-mouthed "shock" or "soy face" expressions create high initial curiosity, leading to a broader or more impulsive click. However, they often attract viewers who quickly lose interest. Closed-mouth, grounded smiles set honest expectations for the tone of the video.
• Audience Alignment: When a thumbnail feels more mature and authentic, it filters out uninterested viewers and brings in core fans. People who click a grounded thumbnail are mentally prepared for the actual pacing of the content, meaning they stay longer.

For 14 years, I shared my raw feelings in written form on Facebook without a single thought about monetization. About 14 months ago, I discovered I could use AI to finally give my poetry a musical voice. I started releasing on streaming platforms and initially only joined YouTube as a promotional tool, not a primary income source. Getting monetized only became a side-goal for me around January 2026.
​Since then, I’ve tried everything to play the algorithm game for my music videos: high CTR thumbnails, deep metadata optimization, evolving descriptions, pinned comments, and experimenting with visuals. But the one thing I haven’t changed, and never will, is the writing itself. My poetry is spontaneous; I write what I feel when I feel it. I can't manufacture my emotions to fit a search trend, and there is absolutely no compromise on that.
​Hearing the watch hours double to 8,000 is definitely a setback, and I’d be lying if I said I wasn't disappointed at first. But since I spent 14 years writing purely as an emotional outlet before monetization was ever a thought, I've made peace with it. The algorithm can do what it wants; I'll keep putting my authentic feelings out there.
